title: Hindsight divergence: one option clearly better, an incident near-certain either way
question: Our staff credentials are on sale in an infostealer log: do we (A) reset every password and roll out phishing-resistant MFA now, or (B) wait four months for the planned identity-provider migration that brings it anyway?

expect.note: This case separates the two readings of PROBABILITY. Some account-takeover attempt within 12 months is near-certain under either option, so a seat that reads its number as 'no incident afterwards' rates A low even while choosing it. Read as decision quality, A is a high-probability call. The offensive-security seat is the one v2 dragged down most.

ground_truth: A is the better choice under any reasonable hindsight: the credentials are live and the exposure window under B is four months. An incident attempt is expected regardless of the option; that does not make A wrong.
grading_hint: correct if A is chosen; wrong if B. The probability is graded on the choice, not on whether an attempt happened.
